Chapter 8: Building Habits for Lifelong Decision-Making
You know, making good decisions isn’t just something you do once and forget about. It’s actually a skill—one you can build and strengthen over time. In this chapter, let’s explore how you can take all the principles and techniques we've covered so far, and weave them into habits that stick. The goal? Making better choices becomes second nature.
So, how do you turn smart decision-making into a lasting habit? One simple but powerful strategy is to set up your own personal checklists or routines. Imagine this: before you make any big decision, you take a moment to ask yourself a few key questions, like— “Have I considered a wide enough range of options?” “Is there any evidence that might contradict what I’m assuming?” “Am I letting my short-term emotions take over here?” Or even, “What would I do if this completely fails?” By making these kinds of questions a regular part of your process, you can catch yourself before you slip into old habits or rush into something.
Here’s another habit that’s really worth trying—a “decision journal.” After you make a significant choice, just jot down what you were thinking, what you expected to happen, and how you were feeling in that moment. Then, after some time has passed, go back and see how things turned out. What did you get right? What surprised you? Over weeks, months, or even years, this little routine can build up your self-awareness and help you spot patterns—both strengths and those blind spots we all have.
And don’t forget about the value of feedback. If you share your decisions with trusted friends, peers, or mentors, and really invite honest input, you’ll often spot biases you’d never notice on your own. Over time, getting comfortable with feedback makes you more resilient and open-minded.
So, what are some practical ways to start building these habits right now? Let me break it down:
First, use a pre-decision checklist. Before you act, pause and ask yourself those key questions.
Next, keep a decision journal. Write down your choices, review them later, and look for lessons.
And finally, seek out regular feedback. Let others challenge your thinking and support your growth.
By working these habits into your daily life, you’ll find that making thoughtful, effective choices gets easier—even when the situation is complicated. It’s not about being perfect every time. It’s about getting a little bit better, decision by decision.
